{{Quote|Anakin's not a Jedi yet, Councilor. He's still a Padawan learner. |Padmé Amidala|<ref name="Episode II">{{Film|II}}</ref>}}
A '''Padawan''', '''Padawan learner''', '''Jedi Apprentice''' in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], or '''Jedi in Training''', referred to a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] adolescent who had begun one-on-one [[Jedi training/Legends|instruction]] with a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] or [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] outside the [[Jedi academy]]. Having passed the [[Initiate Trials/Legends|Initiate Trials]] and ascended in rank from an [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Initiate]], Padawans were given more responsibilities within the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and took part in various missions under the guidance and supervision of their Master.<ref name="The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force real-life book">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>

==Overview==
[[File:Jedi_Initiate.jpg|thumb|left|200px|An Apprentice uses additional technology to amplify her skills in [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] combat.]]
Throughout the early history of the Jedi Order, the role of an apprentice changed drastically as war and purges forced the rule of the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] to bend or become flexible. During and before the [[Old Sith Wars]], Knights and Masters would take on numerous apprentices, training them at their own [[Jedi Praxeum|praxeums]] or private residences without any direct oversight by a council. Using the term ''Apprentice'' to denote their position as a student, many of these students become great Knights and Masters themselves. However it was noted, specifically with the famous incident of [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] and [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]] and their disastrous fall to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]], that this style of education may not be as conducive to the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]] as previously thought.

At some point after the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], the High Council was first convened and set in place the bylaws of the Order. During this period, Masters were restricted to taking only one student at a time. Over time, as the Order flourished, the High Council decided to enforce even stricter standards such as a cut off age for Initiates to be selected for apprenticeship. At the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], which housed the largest of the [[Jedi academy|academies]] of the era, an annual [[Jedi Temple Apprentice Tournament|Apprentice Tournament]] was created to not only test the students at the academy, but also to aid in the selection of apprentices by prospective masters. While it set the rules of the Order, the Masters on the High Council typically avoided direct involvement in this selection, preferring instead to allow [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to bring a Master-Padawan pair together.<ref name="TJP" />

It wasn't until the [[New Sith Wars]] began that the Padawan stage once more fell into disarray as the Order was scattered and formal training halted. With Knights needed at the front, there simply weren't enough teachers to go around; Padawans tended to apprentice for short periods under whoever was available. During the crusades of the [[Army of Light/Legends|Army of Light]], [[Jedi Lord]]s would scour the galaxy for young [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]] that were willing to undergo rudimentary teaching before being thrust into battle with the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]]. Following the victory at [[Ruusan/Legends|Ruusan]] and the following [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Reformations]] in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], the academy on Coruscant was reopened and many of the satellite training academies either shut down or served as secondary facilities in the [[Galactic Rim/Legends|Galactic Rim]].<ref name="TJP" /> <ref name="Star Wars: Knight Errant: Influx">{{SWArchive|url=vault/books/knighterrant_influx/index.html|text=''Star Wars: Knight Errant: Influx''|int=Star Wars: Knight Errant: Influx}}</ref>

In the ensuing [[Golden Age of the Old Republic|Golden Age]], the High Council again became very strict over who was permitted into the Order, with the [[Council of First Knowledge/Legends|Council of First Knowledge]] taking over administration of the academy. However, in rare cases exceptions were made to the age restriction, especially when a well respected Master decided to sponsor a student, as was the case with Master [[Eeth Koth/Legends|Eeth Koth]], who was brought in far past the enforced cut-off.<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> At the end of the Golden Age and the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Order entered into service with the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] and took up military titles. As in past wars, all able-bodied Jedi took to arms, and Padawans were given the rank of [[Jedi Commander/Legends|Commander]] over their troops. Standard procedures were ignored to a lesser degree throughout this conflict, but some small allowances were made in the name of expedience.

[[File:AhsokaAnakin-TCWLD.png|thumb|250px|Most of the Padawan's training took place at their [[Master]]'s side during missions.]]
Many Padawans were promoted faster than was usually viewed as appropriate, and fewer Jedi were being transferred to the [[Jedi Service Corps/Legends|Jedi Service Corps]] than before.<ref name="Yoda: Dark Rendezvous">''[[Yoda: Dark Rendezvous]]''</ref> The tradition ended abruptly in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] when the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], in his guise as [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor of the Republic]], ordered the Grand Army to turn on their Jedi comrades and slay them in accordance with [[Contingency Orders for the Grand Army of the Republic: Order Initiation, Orders 1 Through 150|Executive]] [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]]. With the Order largely destroyed, the newly reorganized [[Stormtrooper Corps/Legends|Stormtrooper Corps]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] were given standing orders to capture any Padawans located during the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] and turn them over to the [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitorius]] for torture and questioning.<ref name="IC">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Commando]]''</ref>

Several decades later, following the defeat of the Sith during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Jedi descendant [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] rebuilt the [[New Jedi Order|Order]] using the basic techniques taught him by the ancient [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]. Not knowing the Order's old regulations, Skywalker erected a [[Jedi Praxeum|Praxeum]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], and gathered any Force-sensitive he could find, regardless of their age. As he built up his Order and gathered more records of the Order from the ruins of the ''[[Chu'unthor]]'' on [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] and recovered [[Holocron/Legends|holocrons]] and [[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force|Temple guidebooks]], Skywalker began to mirror the Old Order's ways and teachings.

Due to the small number of Jedi Knights, Luke Skywalker loosened the restrictions on the number of apprentices a Jedi could train at once. Training his nephews [[Darth Caedus|Jacen]] and [[Anakin Solo]] at the same time, Skywalker saw this technique produce many fine students, but also saw that it took a toll on some of the older students. As the main instructor of several dozen students, Skywalker could not devote as much individual attention to his apprentices, and two succumbed to the pull of the dark side.<ref name="TJP" /> As the Order grew in size, the restrictions began to be reinforced by the reformed [[Jedi High Council (New Jedi Order)|High Council]]. While the term wasn't used Order wide until sometime after the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], the Jedi Trials were once more part of a Jedi's path to Knighthood.<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Revelation">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref>

===Selection===
Throughout the history of the Jedi Order, selection of Padawans has changed based on the state of the academy. While in peacetime, the academy flourished and was maintained by the Council of First Knowledge. The Council placed an age limit on the selection of an Initiate by a master, thus forcing progress amongst students else they join the Service Corps. Encouraging the selection process, the Temple on Coruscant held an annual [[Jedi Temple Apprentice Tournament|tournament]] so that students who had passed the [[Initiate Trials/Legends|Initiate Trials]] could demonstrate their skills with a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] or the Force for visiting Jedi who wished to take an apprentice. In addition to the tournament, many masters looked for references among the academy's [[Jedi instructor|instructors]], hoping to find Jedi proficient in scholarly work and not just skill in combat. On occasion, a master would develop a bond with one of the Temple students and request to become their master; if the apprentice agreed then it was validated by the Council. The Council did not typically get involved in the selection process, yet if a [[Jedi Seer|Seer]] on the Council foresaw a set destiny for a student, they would push them towards fulfilling the prophecy by assigning a student to a master.<ref name="TJP" /> In accordance with their cultural beliefs, [[Mirialan/Legends|Mirialan]] Jedi were only permitted to train if their master was of the same species.<ref name="The Approaching Storm">''[[The Approaching Storm]]''</ref>

When a master selected a student and the Initiate agreed to become an apprentice, the future Padawan would retire to the Coruscant Temple's [[Rotunda chapel|chapel]] for meditation.<ref name="TJP" /> After communing with the Force, the Initiate would report to the Council with their new Master and make a vow to uphold service to the Order, the Force, the Republic, and their master.<ref name="Clone Wars Gambit: Siege">''[[Clone Wars Gambit: Siege]]''</ref>

===Instruction===
{{Main|Jedi training/Legends}}

[[File:Lightsaber_construction.jpg|thumb|left|A Padawan constructs her lightsaber with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].]]
A Padawan accompanied their Master everywhere unless seen unfit by the master, from simple tasks to dangerous missions, so that they learned from experience and personal guidance. Continuing their studies outside the Temple where they had previously spent their entire life, the transition was sometimes difficult but was just one more step along the Jedi path. Depending on their master's specialization, a Padawan would receive shared assignments from one of the four [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Councils]]. All Jedi answered to the High Council and could be deployed on a mission at their behest, expected to apply any number of skills to complete their task. However, some missions were too important to send anyone but a specialist. Following a war with the Sith or an alert to the discovery of a dark side [[Sith artifact/Legends|artifact]], the First Knowledge Council would deploy their agents to recover any dark side imbued talismans or weapons; these agents were responsible for the near annihilation of any mention of the Sith in public documents, practically wiping the memory of the Order's eternal enemies from public mind. Some Jedi worked with the Service Corps, giving their aid to the public or the infirm, or locating and helping new planets enter the Republic.<ref name="TJP" />

In addition to becoming adept with the Force, the Jedi Order expected each Padawan to be as capable as any galactic citizen. Masters taught practical skills like the physical sciences, piloting, droid repair, and astronavigation. Padawans were also taught to be self-sufficient and learned meditations and gardening techniques to stave off hunger.<ref name="Old Republic Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref> Padawans typically maintained the Master-Padawan partnership for a decade, though no set time table was put in place by the Council. Padawans would still take classes at the Temple during their apprenticeship, though their schedules were far more flexible and they were not required to spend time at the Temple to complete a course. Masters could also assign their apprentice to the Temple while they took on a solo mission; during this time a Padawan might take up an additional course or take specialized one-on-one classes with a Temple instructor. While Initiates focused on learning the basics of the [[Force power/Legends|Control]] abilities, Padawans began to learn the intricacies of [[Force sense/Legends|Sense]]. Using the ideas learned from the discipline of Control, Sense was used to sink deeper into the [[Living Force/Legends|Living Force]] and draw upon its energies to use the Force as another "sense".<ref name="TJP" /> 

During the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] period, the focus of Jedi training transformed following the Order's relocation to Tython. In the peaceful years before the [[Great Galactic War]], Padawans were more likely to need an education in the intricacies of [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] politics than Sith warfare. As Jedi began to liaise more frequently with the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic military]], understanding command structures and protocols became essential. While offworld missions had long been a method for broadening students' horizons beyond [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the new era brought a renewed emphasis on practical military readiness and diplomatic service.<ref name="Old Republic Encyclopedia" />

At some point during an apprenticeship, a Padawan was tasked with forging their first lightsaber: one of their sole possessions. After studying the art of lightsaber crafting, a Master-Padawan team would travel to the secret Jedi world, [[Ilum/Legends|Ilum]], and seek out the [[Adegan crystal/Legends|Adegan crystals]] that grew in the [[Crystal Cave/Legends|Jedi Temple]] there. Following a ritual passed from generation to generation, Padawans entered into a deep trance in order to bend matter and create the saber's blade. Often times hallucinations and visions plagued the Jedi while deep in their trance, but these things were considered part of the experience on Ilum. Henceforth, the Padawan would carry their lightsaber everywhere they went, a symbol of their status as Jedi.<ref name="TJP" />

When a master thought that they had taught everything they could, they contacted the High Council to schedule a time for their Padawan to take the [[Jedi Trials/Legends|Jedi Trials]]. Overseen by the Council and the [[Jedi instructor|Temple battlemaster]], the Trials consisted of several tests that were administered in a [[Jedi Trials chamber|specialized chamber]] deep in the Temple. If the Padawan passed each of the Trials, they would ascend to a private, meditation chamber high in the [[Temple Spire/Legends|Tranquillity Spire]]. Following a night of meditation and reflection, the Padawan was summoned to the [[Hall of Knighthood/Legends|Hall of Knighthood]] where the [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] of the Order would [[Knighting Ceremony/Legends|raise]] them to the rank of Knight and sever the Padawan braid. However, if a Padawan failed the test, they were either required to retake them or remain in the Order in the Service Corps. Those Jedi who failed could stay on also as instructors or engineers, maintaining the title of Jedi, while no longer accepting missions from the Council.<ref name="TJP" />

===Dress===
{{Main|Jedi apparel/Legends}}
[[File:Padawan_Robe.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Typical Padawan attire.]]
Like all Jedi, Padawans were expected to wear standard Jedi robes as representatives of the entire Order and its philosophy. While this standard was flexible, based on cultural views, and sometimes disappeared altogether during times of galactic upheaval, the standard was like that of all other Jedi ranks: brown or gray tunic, pants, and robes, with the addition of a leather [[Utility belt/Legends|utility belt]] and boots.<ref name="TJP" />

[[File:AhsokaBonteriEstate.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The unique outfit of Padawan Ahsoka Tano, which included a [[Togruta sash]]]]
The most distinguishing addition to the attire of a Padawan was a small [[Padawan braid/Legends|braid]]. Padawans of hair-growing species were encouraged to grow a single, long, and tight braid of hair (or fur) behind their ear for ease of identifying their rank in the Order, while keeping the rest of their hair short and neat. Often times weaving a ribbon of cloth or special beads into the braid, the lock would be severed upon their ascension to knighthood. For those species that did not grow hair on their head (or at all), alternatives were available. Many bald species such as the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'leks]] or [[Togruta/Legends|Togruta]] wore chains or beads that ran between their [[Lekku/Legends|lekku]] or [[Montral/Legends|montrals]] respectively.<ref name="TJP" />

Some species were recorded to have woven their facial hair into a braid (if they could not grow one from their scalp).<ref name="">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> Other species opted for body modifications such as piercings or markings. [[Sluissi]] Jedi wore a simple tattoo across their left cheek, [[Swokes Swokes/Legends|Swokes Swokes]] could have a medallion implanted below their foreheads, while [[Iktotchi/Legends|Iktotchi]] and [[Chagrian/Legends|Chagrian]] wore circlets on their cranial horns.<ref name="TJP" />

==Behind the scenes==
The term ''Padawan'' first appeared as far back as [[Journal of the Whills, Part I|''Journal of the Whills'', Part I]], [[George Lucas]]'s first story treatment for [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']]. However, it was not heard before [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] was filmed; in all previous works, the concept was called "Apprentice."
